paragraphs.title: Saul Sets Out to Search for David

easy.explanation: The Ziphites came to Saul and told him that David was hiding in the hill of Hachilah.
easy.q: Who told Saul where David was hiding?

easy.explanation: Saul went down to the wilderness of Ziph to seek David.
easy.q: Where did Saul go to search for David?

easy.explanation: Saul went with three thousand chosen men of Israel.
easy.q: How many chosen men of Israel went with Saul?

medium.explanation: David sent out spies and understood that Saul was come in very deed.
medium.q: How did David find out that Saul had truly come into the wilderness?

answers: He came near the place where Saul had pitched
He sent his army to fight Saul
medium.explanation: David arose and came to the place where Saul had pitched.
medium.q: What did David do after learning that Saul had arrived?
In the KJV, what does “abode” mean in “David abode in the wilderness”?

answers: He acted without checking the situation
He was afraid to leave the wilderness
challenge.explanation: David first confirmed that Saul had arrived and only then approached the camp.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David sending out spies?

answers: He used great force to search for one man
challenge.explanation: Saul brought three thousand men to search for David.
challenge.q: Why does Saul’s large army emphasize the seriousness of the pursuit?

answers: David approached, the Ziphites reported, and Saul set out
Saul set out, David sent spies, and David approached the camp
Saul fell asleep, David took the spear, and the Ziphites reported
challenge.explanation: The Ziphites reported David’s location, Saul went out, David sent spies, and then David approached the camp.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is correct?

easy.explanation: Abishai said, “I will go down with thee.”
easy.q: Who went down with David to Saul’s camp?

answers: A spear and a cruse of water
easy.explanation: Saul’s spear and cruse of water were at his bolster.
easy.q: What was beside Saul’s head while he slept?

easy.explanation: Abishai asked permission to smite Saul with the spear.
easy.q: What did Abishai propose to do to Saul?

medium.explanation: David said that no one could stretch forth his hand against the LORD’S anointed and be guiltless.
medium.q: Why did David refuse to harm Saul?

answers: The spear and the cruse of water
medium.explanation: David took Saul’s spear and cruse of water.
medium.q: What did David take from the place?

answers: A man chosen and anointed to be king
A man sent to bring water
medium.explanation: Saul was the king who had been anointed, so David called him the LORD’S anointed.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the LORD’S anointed” refer to?

answers: He trusted the LORD to determine Saul’s fate
He did not believe Saul was dangerous
He wanted to join Saul’s army
challenge.explanation: David said that the LORD would smite Saul, that Saul’s day would come, or that he would perish in battle.
challenge.q: What does David’s decision not to kill Saul reveal about his faith?

answers: They proved David had reached Saul without harming him
They gave David weapons for a large army
They allowed David and Abishai to drink together
challenge.explanation: The objects proved that David had come close enough to kill Saul but chose not to do so.
challenge.q: Why were the spear and cruse of water significant?

answers: Everyone was awake and ready for battle
Everyone was asleep and unaware of them
challenge.explanation: Everyone was asleep because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.
challenge.q: What was unusual about the camp when David and Abishai entered it?

answers: To the other side and the top of a hill
easy.explanation: David went over to the other side and stood on the top of a hill far away.
easy.q: Where did David go after taking the spear and cruse of water?

easy.explanation: David cried to Abner, the son of Ner.
easy.q: Whom did David call from the hill?

answers: A spear and cruse of water
easy.explanation: David showed the king’s spear and the cruse of water.
easy.q: What objects did David display as evidence?

answers: He had not properly guarded the king
medium.explanation: David asked why Abner had not kept his lord the king.

answers: He could speak to them without entering danger again
He wanted to hide the spear
He was searching for the Ziphites
medium.explanation: The distance allowed David to address the camp while remaining out of their reach.
medium.q: Why did David stand far away from the camp?

answers: A place or support near the head
medium.explanation: Saul’s spear and water flask had been placed beside or near his head.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “bolster” mean in this passage?

answers: They proved that Abner had failed to guard Saul
They proved that Abner had defeated David
They proved that Saul had left the kingdom
challenge.explanation: David had taken the objects from beside Saul while Abner and the people failed to notice.
challenge.q: How did the objects strengthen David’s rebuke of Abner?

answers: David approached quietly, while Abner failed to protect the king
David slept, while Abner went to war
David fled, while Abner took the spear
challenge.explanation: Although Abner was the captain of the host, David reached Saul without interference.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between David and Abner?

answers: A speech and rebuke without direct contact
The return of the spear to Abner
challenge.explanation: David could call to the camp from a distance and display the objects as proof.
challenge.q: What did the distance between David and the camp make possible?

paragraphs.title: David Appeals to Saul and Defends His Innocence

easy.explanation: Saul knew David’s voice and asked whether it was his voice.

answers: Why he would not go to battle
easy.explanation: David asked why Saul pursued his servant when he had done no evil.
David compared himself to a flea hunted in the mountains.
easy.q: What did David compare himself to?

answers: That it not fall to the earth before the LORD
That it be given to Abner
That it be kept in the camp
medium.explanation: David asked that his blood not fall to the earth before the face of the LORD.
medium.q: What did David ask concerning his blood?

medium.explanation: David said, “If the LORD have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering.”
medium.q: What did David say should be offered if the LORD had stirred Saul against him?

answers: The land and heritage belonging to the LORD
medium.explanation: The inheritance of the LORD refers to the land and heritage associated with God’s people and worship.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “inheritance” mean in “the inheritance of the LORD”?

answers: He was not an enemy and did not deserve to be pursued
He wanted to become captain of the army
challenge.explanation: David emphasized that he had done no evil and that Saul was pursuing him without just cause.
challenge.q: What was David’s main claim in his speech to Saul?

answers: He presents himself as small and harmless compared with Saul’s pursuit
He claims to be stronger than Saul
He says he is hiding inside the camp
challenge.explanation: A flea is tiny and insignificant, emphasizing the disproportionate nature of Saul’s pursuit.
challenge.q: What does David’s comparison to a flea communicate?

answers: It drove him away from the LORD’S inheritance
It returned him to the hill of Hachilah
challenge.explanation: David said that men had driven him away from abiding in the inheritance of the LORD and told him to serve other gods.
challenge.q: What consequence of the pursuit does David mention?

paragraphs.title: Saul Admits His Wrongdoing and David Moves On

easy.explanation: Saul said, “I have sinned,” and admitted that he had played the fool and erred.

answers: He would no longer harm him
He would immediately give him the kingdom
He would send him to the Ziphites
easy.explanation: Saul promised, “I will no more do thee harm.”
David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
easy.q: What did David do at the end of the passage?

answers: His faithfulness and refusal to harm the LORD’S anointed
His desire to take revenge on Abner
medium.explanation: David said that the LORD would render righteousness and faithfulness, because he had not stretched forth his hand against the LORD’S anointed.
medium.q: What did David emphasize in his answer to Saul?

medium.explanation: Saul said, “Blessed be thou, my son David.”
medium.q: What did Saul say to David after hearing him?

medium.explanation: David appealed to his loyal and upright conduct in refusing to harm Saul.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “faithfulness” mean in David’s statement?

answers: David still went on his way and Saul returned to his place
challenge.explanation: Although Saul confessed and blessed David, the two men separated rather than remaining together.
challenge.q: Why does Saul’s blessing not prove that the conflict was completely resolved?

answers: David maintained distance and left the responsibility to another
David forgot where he found it
David intended to use it against Saul
challenge.explanation: David did not personally return to Saul; he told one of the young men to come and fetch it.
challenge.q: What is suggested by David having a young man fetch the spear?

answers: He refused to harm Saul even when he had the opportunity
He sought a way to replace Abner
He wanted to remain under Saul’s rule
challenge.explanation: David spared Saul, defended his innocence, and repeatedly emphasized that he would not harm the LORD’S anointed.
challenge.q: Which idea best summarizes David’s conduct in this chapter?
